displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that categorical moral obligation is best explained by a necessarily good personal ground, although this abductive conclusion neither follows from moral experience alone nor identifies a particular religion.

novelty.explanation: It replaces a stipulated identity and deductive necessity with a limited abductive thesis grounded in several pro moves.

premises.text: Some moral experiences present themselves not merely as preferences or useful instructions but as categorical reasons that apply despite an agent's contrary desires.

novelty.explanation: It develops the transcript's appeal to immediate obligation while carefully describing its phenomenology rather than assuming objective truth.

premises.text: Evolutionary and cultural explanations of why such experiences arise are compatible with their truth, because a causal genealogy alone does not determine whether their content is warranted.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the global evolutionary defeater by adopting the transcript's stronger causal-versus-justificatory distinction.

premises.text: A complete account of categorical obligation must explain both normative authority and why persons, as deliberating agents, are appropriately addressed by that authority.

novelty.explanation: This is a new agency-centered explanatory criterion not asserted in the locked participant moves.

premises.text: A necessarily good personal foundation may unify value, authority, and accountability more economically than accounts treating normative facts as causally and personally unexplained abstractions.

novelty.explanation: It supplies a comparative explanatory bridge where the transcript had largely stipulated divine grounding.

premises.text: That explanatory advantage is defeasible and depends on showing that divine goodness is principled rather than arbitrary and that competing realist accounts explain less.

novelty.explanation: This newly adds explicit defeasibility and comparative tests that constrain the proposed divine explanation.

conclusion.text: Therefore, categorical moral experience provides qualified abductive support for a necessarily good personal ground if that hypothesis explains authority better than its alternatives, but it does not independently establish Christianity.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion repairs overstatement by making the inference conditional, comparative, and explicitly narrower than a religious identification.

newArguments.title: Second-personal authority
newArguments.text: Moral obligations characteristically address agents as claims that can demand justification, apology, and accountability, not merely as descriptions of optimal conduct. An impersonal moral fact might specify what is valuable, yet leave unexplained why that value authoritatively addresses a person. A necessarily good personal ground could connect value with reason-giving authority without inferring God merely from strong emotion. This argument remains comparative: it succeeds only if impersonal realism, constructivism, and social accounts cannot explain second-personal authority equally well.

novelty.explanation: The second-personal structure of obligation is a genuinely new reinforcing argument absent from the participant's locked moves.

newArguments.title: Evolution without global skepticism
newArguments.text: An evolutionary genealogy need not defeat every belief. The narrower challenge asks whether a disposition would have promoted fitness across many incompatible moral propositions and whether reflective checking independently discriminates among them. If a particular moral seeming remains stable under information, impartial perspective-taking, coherence testing, and exposure to counterexamples, its genealogy alone supplies no decisive defeater. This approach preserves the pro concern about reliability while abandoning the unsupported claim that evolutionary causation automatically discredits all cognition.

novelty.explanation: It reconstructs the evolutionary challenge as a local defeater analysis instead of the transcript's unsupported global skepticism.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that moral experience can be explained and practically disciplined through conscious interests, social coordination, and reflective procedures without establishing mind-independent value or a divine moral ground.

novelty.explanation: It integrates the con side's psychological, evolutionary, and inferential points into a proportionate nondeductive thesis.

premises.text: Evolution, learning, empathy, and social dependence plausibly explain why humans possess powerful dispositions concerning harm, reciprocity, loyalty, and cooperation.

novelty.explanation: It develops the transcript's evolutionary explanation by adding learning and social dependence without changing its causal role.

premises.text: The intensity, convergence, or involuntary character of a moral seeming does not by itself establish that its content is true independently of every valuing mind.

novelty.explanation: It combines the transcript's distinction between compelling experience and objective status with its warning about emotional inference.

premises.text: Causal explanations of moral experience and justificatory procedures for revising conduct answer different questions, so explaining origins need not pretend to prove objective moral properties.

novelty.explanation: It preserves and broadens the con side's strongest explicit causal-versus-normative distinction.

premises.text: Public standards can be constructed through informed agreement, consistency, reciprocity, and protection against domination, even when their authority remains dependent on conscious agents and shared practices.

novelty.explanation: This procedural constructivist account is a new line that supplies practical authority beyond the transcript's conditional survival rules.

premises.text: Invoking God does not improve the explanation unless independent evidence supports that being and a noncircular account connects divine nature with reasons binding human agents.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the categorical circularity objection by stating conditional explanatory requirements rather than assuming no independent divine case exists.

conclusion.text: Therefore, moral experience does not presently require a divine or mind-independent ground; a conscious-agent and procedural account remains viable while leaving broader metaphysical possibilities open.

novelty.explanation: It limits the conclusion to explanatory viability and underdetermination instead of claiming that the transcript proved subjectivism.

newArguments.title: Procedural moral authority
newArguments.text: Subject dependence need not reduce morality to each individual's momentary preference. Agents can ask which rules informed persons could justify to one another under conditions protecting voice, consistency, reciprocity, and freedom from coercive domination. Standards produced through that procedure remain grounded in conscious interests, yet they can criticize existing consensus and personal desire. The account explains moral revision without positing stance-independent properties: reforms occur when excluded interests become visible, factual errors are corrected, or accepted principles are applied more consistently.

novelty.explanation: This procedural constructivist argument is genuinely new and supplies a nonarbitrary source of criticism absent from the live exchange.

newArguments.title: Explanatory underdetermination
newArguments.text: Even if objective obligation were granted, the inference to God would remain underdetermined. Irreducible normative realism, naturalist realism, ideal-observer theories, and constructivist accounts offer different explanations of apparent authority. A divine hypothesis gains support only after comparative criteria are specified and those alternatives perform worse. Thus the con side need not prove that every divine ground is impossible; it can require the pro side to show why personality, necessity, and perfect goodness are explanatory consequences rather than attributes inserted to reproduce the moral data.

novelty.explanation: It strengthens the inference-gap objection through explicit comparative alternatives while avoiding the transcript's overstrong circularity claim.
